Performers
Alain Fauqueur (boy soprano; Petits Chanteurs de Vincennes), J. J. Grunenwald (organ), Orchestre des Concerts Lamoureux (instrumental players for the chamber scoring), Igor Markevitch (conductor) Documented

Per-work soloist headings were visually read, not inferred from a whole-album creator tag. Markevitch is the conductor; Nadia Boulanger is separately credited with recording supervision. J. J. Grunenwald is named only for the works whose scores contain organ. The ensemble credits are album-level; individual instrumental players and exact section numbers are unestablished.

[4] [12] [6] [2]
Work version
Complete original chamber scoring for high solo voice, two violins, viola, cello, harp and organ; sung here by a boy soprano. Documented

The consulted Durand score is a later impression of the original 1922 edition, not evidence of the session’s actual performing copy. The quartet and harp players are not individually named.

[12] [7] [8]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

No dated session log was established. The 1960 release year, 2021 transfer date and 2023 derivative-generation date are not recording dates.

[2] [3] [1]
Place
Salle Pleyel, Paris, France Documented

The sleeve explicitly states that the recording was made at the Salle Pleyel on Everest equipment; this is not inferred from the orchestra’s home city.

[2] [3]
Label
Everest Documented

Original mono LP imprint; the original copyright credit is Belock Instrument Corp.

[2] [3] [1]
Catalogue
LPBR 6059 (mono LP) Documented

SDBR 3059 is the separately identified stereo counterpart, not the transferred catalogue number.

[2] [3] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Side B4; Discogs reports the corresponding side runout LPBR-6059-2-T1. Documented

Track/side position is documented. The reported runout belongs to the catalogued release; the transferred specimen’s runout was not physically inspected. No session matrix, take number or meaning of the T1 suffix is established.

[3] [2]
Transfer
Internet Archive; workstation archivelp-rip-cebu19. Documented

This is the explicit ripping_operator credit, not the item’s separate uploader/operator. A restoration or mastering engineer is not identified.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-09-18 Documented

ripping_date is 20210918003915. The calendar date is reported without inventing a timezone; added/public dates and later derivative timestamps are not substituted.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable + Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; ArchiveCD Version 2.2.57lp. Original side FLAC files are retained, with segmented VBR MP3 access derivatives. Documented

The chain is transcribed from lineage and ripping_software_version. The selected MP3’s original pointer names the segments JSON. De-clicking, equalisation, noise reduction, original session tape format and any intermediate mastering are not documented; none is asserted.

[1]
Composition rights
Boulanger’s music is out of copyright under the ordinary EU life-plus-70 term. Inferred, not documented

Boulanger died in 1918. This is a territorial term calculation for the original music, not a worldwide clearance or a claim about an unidentified modern edition. The biblical or liturgical text is not used as evidence for the sound-recording rights.

[9] [7] [10]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU sound-recording public domain: lawful publication documented by 1960, before 1963. Documented

The original commercial mono release LPBR 6059 is dated 1960; the sleeve carries ©1960 Belock, corroborated by the label discography. The rule concerns first lawful publication anywhere, not first EU publication. On the former fifty-year term this phonogram was no longer protected before the 2013 extension. US recording status is not established. No worldwide public-domain claim, Creative Commons licence or modern-remaster release is inferred.

[2] [3] [5] [11]

Lili Boulanger, Pie Jesu; Alain Fauqueur, boy soprano; J. J. Grunenwald, organ; members of the Orchestre des Concerts Lamoureux; Igor Markevitch, conductor. Everest LPBR 6059, side B4, published 1960; recorded at Salle Pleyel, session date unestablished. Internet Archive vinyl transfer, ripping date 18 September 2021. Territorial EU rule 3; US recording status not established. Rights statement

Grunenwald; named soloist roster; recording direction Nadia Boulanger. Psalm 130’s individual heading names Oralia Dominguez and Raymond Amade.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. David Edwards and Mike Callahan — Everest Classical Album Discography — 2018 discography, p. 5: LPBR 6059 mono / SDBR 3059 stereo, [1960], Boulanger programme. Corroborates the sleeve’s publication-year evidence, not a session date.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Everest — SDBR 3059 programme and per-track credits — Official stereo counterpart page identifies Dominguez and Amade for Psalm 130; Sénéchal for Psalm 24 and Vieille prière; Mollet for Psalm 129; Fauqueur for Pie Jesu. This corroborates the visually inspected mono insert; the stereo stream is not used.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Lili Boulanger — original Durand full score — Printed pp. 2–⁠7. Quartet icons represent individual string players, not orchestral sections. The exact performing edition and unnamed string/harp players are unestablished. Representative passage snapshots, placed approximately using the cached level/novelty report and score order. Not continuous player detection; individual rests are not mapped.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. IMSLP — work and publication record — General Information: composition and publication dates, scoring, text and work identity. The linked original full score was opened and visually inspected; this catalogue page alone is not used to infer instrumental entrances.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Library of Congress — Lili Boulanger — Biographical dates 1893–⁠1918; first woman to win the composition Prix de Rome in 1913; Villa Medici and the sisters’ wartime support work.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. Directive 2006/116/EC — term of protection — Articles 1 and 8: ordinary authorial life-plus-70 term and calculation from the following 1 January; Article 3’s historical phonogram term is read with the 2011 extension’s transition rule. Recording and composition rights remain separate.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  11. Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram extension and transition — Article 1 amendments: extended phonogram protection applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. The 1960 publication evidence puts this recording’s former fifty-year term before that transition. This is a territorial EU basis, not a worldwide licence or US clearance.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  12. Everest LPBR 6059 — visually inspected per-track insert — Individual work heading supplies the named soloist for Pie Jesu. Notes by David Noakes; ©1960 Belock footer on the final insert leaf. For Psalm 129, the preceding continuation on the last leaf describes women’s wordless closing voices.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
